newsitem.title: USA: Tandem to sell arm to Newbridge.
newsitem.headline: Tandem to sell arm to Newbridge.

text.p: Tandem Computers Inc. said Thursday it agreed to sell its computer networking equipment unit, UB Networks, to Newbridge Networks Corp. for an undisclosed sum.

The sale, expected to close in 30 days, will help Tandem concentrate on its fault-tolerant computer business and will help Newbridge Networks, a computer networking equipment maker, expand its product lines, the companies said.

The stock of Tandem, based in Cupertino, Calif., fell 62.5 cents to $14 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Shares of Newbridge Networks, based in Kanata, Ontario, were unchanged on the Toronto Stock Exchange at C$40.40 ($29.50). On the NYSE, Newbridge stock fell 12.5 cents to $29.50.
David Rynne, Tandem chief financial officer, said he expected Tandem to report a "modest" gain in the quarter ended in March after the completion of the sale.

Tandem specialises in making computers that handle huge volumes of transactions, such as stock trades and telephone billing. The company bought UB Networks for about $260 million in 1988 to get networking gear that would let its computers share information with other machines.
With the proliferation of networking equipment companies in the past five years, it is "less strategically important to have your own communication division," Rynne said.
In the most recent fiscal year, ended Sept. 30, UB Networks lost $17.3 million on revenues of $377 million.
Newbridge Networks said it planned to take advantage of UB Networks' strong sales force and customer support to win more accounts from global companies.
Christopher Brennan will continue as president and chief operating officer of UB Networks, Newbridge Networks said.
